LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

ORDER NUMBER U-37584 

MAGNOLIA WATER UTILITY 
OPERATING COMPANY, LLC, EX PARTE 

Docket No. U-37584, In re: Request for extension of Formula Rate Plan. 
(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session.) 

ORDER 
Background and Overview 
In this proceeding, Magnolia Water Utility Operating Company, LLC (“Magnolia” or the 
“Applicant”) is seeking a renewal and extension of its Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”). Magnolia’s 
initial FRP, approved by the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission” or “LPSC”) in 
Order No. U-35822,1 began with test year 2022 and expired with test year 2024, having a Return 
on Equity (“ROE”) bandwidth of 9.00% to 10.00% and a 9.50% ROE midpoint.2 Magnolia seeks 
an extension of its FRP in its entirety. 
Commission Staff recommends that Magnolia be authorized to renew its FRP for an 
additional three-year term under the same terms and conditions as in its previously approved FRP, 
with certain language modifications and changes to its capital structure requirements. Intervenors 
in the docket, who are Magnolia customers, oppose Magnolia’s request. Generally, the Intervenors 
contend that Magnolia’s annual FRP filings, and Commission Staff’s analysis thereof, were 
incomplete and based on unsubstantiated financial reports of expenses and repairs. 

Pertinent Procedural History 
On May 16, 2025, Magnolia filed with the Commission a Request for Extension of Formula 
Rate Plan, with attached testimony in support (the “Request”). The Request was published in the 
Commission’s Official Bulletin on May 23, 2025, with a 15-day intervention period. There were 
twenty-five timely interventions.3 A status conference on the matter was held on July 8, 2025, at 
which a procedural schedule was established.

Application for Approval of Rate Design, Increase in Water and Sewerage Rates, Implementation of Service Charges 
and Any Other Related Relief. 
2 Magnolia’s Request for Extension of Formula Rate Plan at 2 (Magnolia Hr’g Ex. 1).

Brandon Tull, and Gilda Washington. Arthur Laughlin withdrew his intervention on August 20, 2025, and George 
Haase withdrew his intervention on December 1, 2025.

7, 2025, Intervenor Cindy Case-Brown filed her direct testimony/comments. On October 13, 2025,

On January 27, 2026, individual pre-hearing statements were filed by Commission Staff, 
Magnolia, Ms. Case-Brown, and Ms. Pautler. On January 28, 2026, a Notice of Required Filing

Case-Brown, and Ms. Pautler. A hearing on the merits was convened on February 9, 2025. A 
Notice of Availability of Transcript and Notice of Post-Hearing Briefing Schedule was issued on 
March 10, 2026. On March 30, 2026, Ms. Case-Brown filed her post-hearing brief. On March 31, 
2026, post-hearing briefs were filed individually by Magnolia and Commission Staff. On April 1, 
2026, Ms. Norris filed her post-hearing brief and Separate Findings of Fact.4,5 On April 13, 2026, 
Ms. Case-Brown filed two reply briefs responding separately to Commission Staff and Magnolia. 
On April 14, 2026, Magnolia, Commission Staff, and Ms. Norris each individually filed their post-

4 The filing deadline for post-hearing briefs was March 31, 2026, and Ms. Norris filed hers on April 1, 2026. No party

5 In her post-hearing filings, Ms. Norris included findings of fact. Rule 55(o) of the Commission’s Rules of Practice

any proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law are not considered in the adjudication of this docket.

The Administrative Law Judge issued a Proposed Recommendation on May 6, 2026. On 
May 14, 2026, Ms. Case-Brown filed her Exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation. On May 
20, 2026, Ms. Norris filed her Exceptions and Opposition to the Proposed Recommendation. On 
May 21, 2026, Magnolia filed its Oppositions to the Exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation. 
The Final Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge was issued on June 10, 2026. The 
Commission considered the Final Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge at its June 
17, 2026 Business and Executive Session. After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, 
seconded by Commissioner Francis, with Vice Chairman Coussan and Commissioner Lewis 
concurring, and Commissioner Campbell absent, the Commission voted to approve the Final 
Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge filed into the record on June 10, 2026. 

Jurisdiction and Applicable Law 
Pursuant to the Louisiana Constitution, Article 4, Section 21, the Commission shall 
regulate all common carriers and public utilities, and adopt and enforce reasonable rules, 
regulations, and procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties. La. R.S. 45:1163(A)(1) 
provides that the Commission shall exercise all necessary power and authority over any electric

title: Order No. S-37857 — Utility Order for National Water Infrastructure, LLC, ex parte.
text:
Order No. S-37857 
Page 1 
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

ORDER NUMBER S-37857 

NATIONAL WATER INFRASTRUCTURE, LLC, EX PARTE. 

Docket No. S-37857, In re: Request for Letter of Non-Opposition to enter into certain credit 
facilities, issue guarantees, and grant security interests in its assets in connection with the credit 
facilities. 

(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session.) 

ORDER 

I. 

Overview 
On February 24, 2026, National Water Infrastructure, LLC (“NWI” or the “Company”) filed 
the above-captioned request (“Request”) pursuant to the Louisiana Public Service Commission’s 
(“LPSC” or the “Commission”) General Order dated November 13, 1996 (“1996 General Order”)1 
and General Order dated March 18, 1994 (“1994 General Order”).2 The Request sought the 
Commission's non-opposition to NWI entering into certain Credit Facilities. These Credit Facilities 
would consist of an eighteen (18) month interim non-revolving construction line of credit with an 
aggregate principal amount of up to $50 million (the “Interim Construction Loan”) and a thirty-six (36) 
month revolving line of credit in an amount of up to $6 million outstanding at any time, (the 
“Revolver”). The Interim Construction Loan and Revolver (Credit Facilities) would be issued by 
Hancock Whitney Bank as the Lender with National Water Infrastructure Holdings, LP (“NWI 
Holdings”), among other related entities of NWI, as guarantors under the Credit Facilities. NWI 
Holdings is an affiliate of NWI through ultimate common ownership by Bernhard Capital Partners 
(“BCP”). 
The proceeds from the Interim Construction Loan would allow NWI to finance start of 
construction of the Central Treatment Plant that the Commission approved for NWI to consolidate and 
regionalize wastewater collection and treatment systems in Ascension Parish (the “Regionalization 
Project”), pursuant to Order No. U-36383, dated September 13, 2023 (the “Order”). According to the 
Order, NWI has and will continue to pursue financing pursuant to the Environmental Protection 
Agency’s (“EPA”) Wastewater Infrastructure and Innovation Act (“WIFIA”) program for the most 
favorable terms available to reduce customer costs associated with the Regionalization Project. Due to 
delays in receiving the WIFIA funding, the Company now requires the Credit Facilities to proceed with 
the construction of the Central Treatment Plant. The Interim Construction Loan will be repaid by 17 
monthly interest-only payments, with all unpaid and accrued interest and principal due at maturity. 
NWI anticipates that any outstanding balance of the Interim Construction Loan will be paid in full and 
the loan canceled once funding is obtained through the WIFIA program. 
The proceeds from the Revolver will be used to fund general corporate activities, including 
without limitation, working capital needs, capital expenditures, acquisitions, and other purposes 

1 In re: Commission approval of security issues and assumptions of liability. 
2 In re: Commission approval required of sales, leases, mergers, consolidations, stock transfers, and all other 
changes of ownership or control of public utilities subject to Commission jurisdiction. 

Order No. S-37857 
Page 2 
as permitted by the Lender. The Revolver will be repaid with 35 monthly interest-only payments, 
with all unpaid accrued interest and principal due at maturity. 
NWI indicated that the proceeds of the Credit Facilities will also be used to pay in full any 
outstanding balance of the J.P. Morgan Chase Bank revolving line of credit facility that was previously 
approved by the Commission pursuant to Order No. S-36363, dated August 26, 2022. 
NWI has also indicated that the Credit Facilities will not result in material changes to the 
Company's current credit profile or capital structure and that the Credit Facilities will be secured by a 
first priority multiple indebtedness mortgage on the Company’s Ascension Parish property on which 
the Central Treatment Plant will be constructed for the Regionalization Project, a first priority UCC 
security interest on all assets of the Company (excluding titled vehicles), an assignment of all leases 
and rents on the Company’s Ascension Parish Property on which the Central Treatment Plant will be 
constructed, and guarantees by NWI Holdings and other related entities of NWI. 
The Request was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin No. 1370 on February 
27, 2026, for a fifteen-day (15-day) intervention period. No interventions were received during or 
subsequent to the intervention period. 
NWI is a Louisiana limited liability company ultimately owned and controlled by BCP, with 
its main office located at 37458 Cornerview Road, Geismar, Louisiana 70734. NWI operates as a water 
and wastewater utility in Louisiana subject to the Commission’s jurisdiction and currently provides 
wastewater utility services to residential and commercial customers in Ascension, Calcasieu, East 
Baton Rouge, Iberville, Livingston, Point Coupee, St. Tammany, Tangipahoa, and West Baton Rouge 
Parishes and water utility services to customers in Calcasieu Parish. NWI provides service to 
approximately 24, 241 residential and commercial ratepayers.3 

II. 
Jurisdiction and Applicable Law 
The Commission exercises jurisdiction over public utilities in Louisiana, including NWI, 
pursuant to Article IV, Section 21(B) of the Louisiana Constitution, which states the following: 
The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public 
utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by 
law. It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations and 
procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall 
have other powers and perform other duties as provided by law. 

Pursuant to its constitutional authority, the Commission promulgated the 1996 General 
Order, which provides in pertinent part the following: 
No public utility shall issue any security or assume any obligation 
or liability as guarantor, endorser, surety or otherwise in respect of 
any security of any other public utility, or of any person, until it has 
been authorized to do so by Order of this Commission. 
* * * 
The Commission shall not approve any issue or assumption of any 
security, obligation or liability, unless, after investigation of the 
purposes and uses of the proposed issue and the proceeds thereof, 
or of the proposed assumption of obligation or liability, the 

3 These calculations are derived from NWI’s 2025 Annual Report submitted to the Commission April 30, 2026. 

Order No. S-37857 
Page 3 
Commission finds that the issue or assumption is for some lawful 
object within the corporate purposes of the public utility, it is 
necessary or appropriate for or consistent with the performance by 
the public utility of its service to the public and will not impair its 
ability to perform that service, and it is consistent with the public 
interest and the best interest of ratepayers. 
* * * 
This General Order does not modify in any manner the General 
Order issued by this Commission dated 3/18/94 related to 
Commission approval of sales, leases, etc. Any security issuance 
that requires a utility to "sell, assign, lease, transfer, mortgage, or 
otherwise dispose of or encumber" the property or assets of the 
utility must be approved by the Commission under the standards 
set forth in the 3/18/94 General Order as well.4 
In accordance with its constitutional authority, the Commission also promulgated the 1994 
General Order, which provides in pertinent part the following: 
No utility or common carrier subject to the jurisdiction of the 
Louisiana Public Service Commission shall … mortgage, or 
otherwise … encumber the whole or any part of its franchise, works, 
property, or system, … where the values involved in such action 
exceed one percent (1%) of the gross assets of such regulated utility 
or common carrier, or subsidiary thereof, nor in any way commit 
itself to take such action or affect any right, interest, asset, obligation, 
stock ownership, or control, involved in such action without prior full 
disclosure of the prior intendment and plan of such utility or common 
carrier with regard to such action and without prior official action of 
approval or official action of non-opposition by the Louisiana 
Public Service Commission.5 
The Commission's 1994 General Order also sets forth eighteen (18) factors which the 
Commission shall take into account in determining whether to approve a transaction coming within 
the General Order’s scope.6 

III. 

NWI’s Request 
In its Request, NWI sought a Letter of Non-Opposition to enter into certain Credit Facilities in 
the aggregate amount of up to $56 million dollars from the Lender for general corporate activities and 
more precisely to finance start of construction of the Central Treatment Plant while anticipated long-
term funding from WIFIA for the Regionalization Project is pending. Staff noted that the total Interim 
Construction Loan is significantly less than what NWI anticipates the full Regionalization Project 
would cost. NWI has indicated that it expects a variable rate equal to 175 basis points over the 
applicable AMERIBOR Term-30 rate. NWI anticipates taking monthly withdrawals from the Credit 
Facilities based on actual invoices related to the Regionalization Project and is expecting funding from 
WIFIA to relieve the full amount attributed to the Interim Construction Loan. NWI anticipates interest 
only payments on the Credit Facilities until such a time that they mature or are paid in full due to 
WIFIA funding. 

4 1996 General Order, supra note 1, ordering paras. 1,3, 5. 
5 1994 General Order, supra note 2, ordering para. 1. 
6 See, 1994 General Order, supra note 2, ordering para. 2. 

Order No. S-37857 
Page 4 
In support of its Request, NWI provided responses to formal data requests from Staff, an 
eighteen-factor (18-factor) analysis pursuant to the Commission's 1994 General Order and summaries 
of the anticipated indicative terms and conditions relating to the Credit Facilities. Additionally, NWI 
filed a supplemental filing on April 23, 2026 which included refinements to the Lender’s loan 
commitments. In addition to what was submitted into the record by NWI, Audit Staff sought additional 
information through various formal data requests to ascertain additional details about how the proceeds 
from the Credit Facilities would be used, costs, be reimbursed, and be drawn by the Company. NWI 
asserted that the proposed transaction is in the best interest of the public, as it is necessary and 
appropriate for, and consistent with the performance by the Company of its services to the public and 
would not impair its ability to perform such services. 

IV. 

Staff Review and Recommendation 
Staff conducted a thorough review of NWI's Request, and all supporting documentation, 
supplemental filings, responses to data requests, as well as the settlement terms of its last rate case in 
Docket U-36383. Staff’s Report and Recommendation was filed into the record on May 27, 2026. The 
Company filed a non-opposition to the Staff Report and Recommendation on May 29, 2026. 
Staff noted its understanding that the Request is a means for NWI to start construction of the 
Regionalization Project that was approved in Order No. U-36383 dated September 13, 2023, and is meant 
to be a temporary stop-gap in funding while NWI finishes out the EPA’s WIFIA program application for 
more favorable long-term funding for the overall Project. Staff’s review highlighted that the total amount 
being sought by NWI through the Credit Facilities is only a portion of the overall Regionalization 
Project’s anticipated construction cost. Additionally, as part of the settlement terms in Order No. U-
36383, NWI has an established route to assist in cost recovery through the filing which incorporates rate 
payer protections in the form of a rate cap structure of no more than a $10 per month (“Rate Cap”) in any 
resulting year for construction work in progress (“CWIP”). 
Staff’s review highlighted on the Credit Facilities and believes that the terms and conditions 
therein are reasonable and the interest only payment structure would be favorable to NWI and its 
ratepayers until such time that the WIFIA program funds are realized and the Interim Construction Loan 
portion of the Credit Facilities would be paid in full for more favorable long-term funding. Staff's review 
of interest rates associated with the Credit Facilities indicated that they are well-established market rates. 
The timing of NWI’s Request is in-line with the expected construction start timeline beginning 
in June 2026 and NWI indicated that it believes the WIFIA program request would be finalized and 
completed prior to the end of the maturity period for the Interim Construction Loan portion of the Credit 
Facilities. Additionally, NWI would make monthly draws instead of a single lump sum which would be 
dependent upon actual work invoices from the Regionalization Project. NWI would be responsible 
for interest only payments until maturity or until the total is repaid in full using the WIFIA program 
funds. 
Finally, as this transaction is subject to the 1994 General Order, Staff reviewed NWI’s 
responses to the eighteen-factor (18-factor) analysis. The Company stated there will not be a 
transfer of ownership under the proposed transaction. NWI further contended that the transaction 
is in the best interest of ratepayers based on the following points: 

Order No. S-37857 
Page 5 
• The Proposed Transaction would serve the public interest by enhancing NWI’s 
ability to continue providing safe and reliable wastewater utility services to its 
Louisiana Customers, would not result in the loss or impairment of service to any 
customers, and not affect the Commission’s exercise of its regulatory authority over 
the Company. 
• That ratepayers would see both short and long-term benefits such as safety and 
reliability benefits and environmental benefits from the Regionalization Project, the 
rate protections set up through the Rate Cap, as well as the long-term benefits of the 
WIFIA program funding that will assist in overall costs for the Regionalization 
Project. 
• The Proposed Transaction would not adversely affect NWI’s ability to maintain 
and/or acquire any necessary health, safety or other permits and that NWI would 
be able to proceed with the agreed upon construction as outlined in the Order. 

In summary, NWI provided Staff with an in-depth look at the Company’s financials and 
motives behind the Request. Staff believes the Request provides NWI with favorable and 
commercially reasonable terms that will allow the Company to begin construction of the 
Regionalization Project. The Order details a cost recovery mechanism that was agreed upon by the 
LPSC and instills a number of ratepayer protections moving forward, including the Rate Cap 
component. 
Based on the foregoing, Staff found that NWI’s Request is for a lawful object within the 
Company’s corporate purposes, is necessary and appropriate for and consistent with NWI’s 
performance of its service to the public, will not impair NWI’s ability to perform that service, and is 
consistent with the public interest and the best interest of ratepayers. Accordingly, Staff recommended 
that the Commission express its non-opposition to the Request subject to the following conditions: 
1. The Company shall file into the record of this proceeding a copy of the signed and executed 
terms and conditions of the Credit Facilities as well as any related instruments and 
documentation within thirty (30) days of the loan closing date. 

2. If the Credit Facilities are modified in any way prior to issuance of funds, the modified 
agreements shall be filed into the record of this proceeding no later than fifteen (15) days 
after such modification. 

3. If a copy of the signed and executed documents have not been filed within ninety (90) days 
of the issuance of an order in this proceeding, the Company shall file a status update on the 
loan closing into the record of this proceeding on or before ninety (90) days from the 
issuance of an order in this proceeding. 

4. Until the maturity of the Interim Construction Loan, the Company shall file into the record of 
this proceeding a report every six (6) months highlighting the amount drawn down, the 

Order No. S-37857 
Page 6 
construction work completed, and any efforts regarding the WIFIA program. The report shall 
include the total amount budgeted for that period, the total amount spent, the remaining totals 
for work to be done, and a timeline for completion of that work. Such reports shall be filed by 
January 31 and July 31 or the first day immediately following those dates when the 
Commission’s office in Baton Rouge, Louisiana is open for business pursuant to Rule 5 of the 
Commission’s Rules of Practices and Procedures. 

5. The Commission specifically reserves its right to rescind its non-opposition if any of the 
above conditions are not satisfied. 

6. The Commission expresses its non-opposition without prejudice to the Commission’s 
authority to make any investigation and require any reasonably necessary change that the 
Commission may legally find to be in the public interest. 

V. 

Commission Consideration 
This matter was considered at the Commission’s June 17, 2026 Business and Executive 
Session. After discussion, on motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, 
with Commissioner Lewis and Commissioner Francis concurring, and Commissioner Campbell 
absent, the Commission voted to accept the Staff Report and Recommendation filed into the record 
on May 27, 2026.

That the Louisiana Public Service Commission expresses its non-opposition to the

down, the construction work completed, and any efforts regarding the WIFIA program. 
The report shall include the total amount budgeted for that period, the total amount

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

ORDER NUMBER T-37789 

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
VERSUS 
RODNEY DUPRE, JR. DBA JACE’S TOWING & TRANSPORT 

Docket No. T-37789, In re: Alleged violation of (1) 45:161 through 180.1 and General Order 
dated November 8, 1999, by operating Intrastate without LPSC authority and (2) General Order 
dated December 20, 2024 for exceeding state prescribed rates, allegedly having occurred on or 
about October 04, 2025. 

(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session.) 

ORDER 

Overview 
The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) issued a citation 
dated November 25, 2025, to Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s Towing & Transport (“Jace’s Towing” 
or the “Carrier”). The citation directs the Carrier to appear at a hearing on February 3, 2026, to 
show cause why it should not be found guilty as alleged in the In re. The citation was docketed as 
the instant proceeding and notice of this proceeding was published in the Commission’s Official 
Bulletin dated December 5, 2025. When the hearing was convened on February 3, 2026, 
Commission Staff appeared through counsel and presented testimonial and documentary evidence 
in support of its allegations. The Carrier did not appear at the hearing. For the reasons stated herein, 
we find Jace’s Towing guilty as alleged. 

The Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge (Corrected) (“Recommendation”) 
was issued in the form of a Draft Order on June 5, 2026. The Recommendation was considered at 
the Commission’s Business and Executive Session held on June 17, 2026. On motion of 
Commissioner Lewis, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, with Chairman Skrmetta concurring 
and Commissioner Campbell absent, the Commission accepted the Recommendation. 
Applicable Law 

The Commission exercises jurisdiction in this proceeding pursuant to Article IV, Section 
21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which provides in pertinent part: 
The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public 
utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. 
It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and 
procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and perform 
other duties as provided by law. 

In addition, the Louisiana Legislature, in La. R.S. 45:163, delegates certain authority to the 
Commission over motor carriers operating intrastate in Louisiana. La. R.S. 45:162(12) includes 
tow trucks in the definition of “motor carriers” subject to the Commission’s regulation. More 
specifically, the Louisiana Legislature has declared, in La. R.S. 45:180.1, that the “use and 
operation of wreckers and towing services should be the subject of regulation by the Louisiana 
Public Service Commission,”1 and that the Commission has “the power and authority necessary to 
supervise, govern, regulate, and control the business of the operation and use of wreckers and 
towing services . . . [and] to fix reasonable and just rates, fares, tolls, charges for storage services 

1 La. R.S. 45:180.1(B). 
Order No. T-37789 
Page 2 of 11 
. . . .”2 In accordance with La. R.S. 45:171(A), no carrier shall violate the provisions of Title 45, 
Chapter 4 (which includes La. R.S. 45: 180.1) or any Commission order. La. R.S. 45:180.1 states 
that in addition to any other penalties imposed by Chapter 4, no person shall violate Section 180.1 
or engage in the operation and use of wreckers and towing services without first having obtained 
authority from the Commission. La. R.S. 45:171(C) and La. R.S. 45:180.1(E) state that violators 
shall be fined by the Commission at open hearing not less than $100 and not more than $10,000. 

Pursuant to these delegations of authority, the Commission adopted rules applicable to 
wrecker and towing services providing nonconsensual towing and recovery services. The 
Commission’s General Order dated November 8, 1999 (“1999 General Order”),3 adopted 
guidelines for nonconsensual wrecker and towing services, including an application process. 
Section II, General Requirements for Wrecker and Towing Services within the State of Louisiana, 
states that an application will be submitted, and upon Staff approval applicants must comply with 
the requirements of R.S. 45:161 through 172 before a certificate or permit will be issued. Section 
II also specifies the insurance requirements. While Section II of the 1999 General Order remains 
intact, the rates and terms applicable to nonconsensual towing and recovery services have been 
amended many times since the issuance of the 1999 General Order. 

The most recent General Order addressing nonconsensual towing and recovery service 
rates is the Commission’s General Order dated December 20, 2024 (“Towing Order”).4 Amended 
Attachment A to the Towing Order includes the schedule of the rates and terms for nonconsensual 
towing and recovery services applicable to Commission-jurisdictional carriers. Included therein at 
Section VII, Annual Producer Price Index Adjustment, it states that the LPSC’s rates will be 
increased or decreased annually based on the Producer Price Index (“PPI”), that the rate change 
will be posted on the Commission’s website each April 1, and that the rates will become effective 
upon posting. Pursuant to the Towing Order, the rates and terms that apply to the tow at issue in 
this proceeding are found in Amended Attachment A for 2024 PPI to the General Order updated 
on April 1, 2025 (“2025 Towing Order Rates”).5 The most pertinent terms and rates to the issues 
of the case are as follows:

1. A Tow Company shall only charge the rates stated in this order and fees allowed by

2. All rates for towing, recovery, and stand-by in Section II.A and B include the truck and

3. A Tow Company shall only charge for equipment and personnel that are present at the

4. The Commission’s jurisdiction is from the time that the towing or recovery unit is

shall not charge any rate other than those specified in this order , for removal of debris

to prevent fuel from leaking during towing and billed pursuant to Section B.

B. In addition to any fines authorized by La. R.S. Title 45 or Commission Orders, the 
Commission may order a refund of up to 200% of any overcharges. 

VII. 
ANNUAL PRODUCER PRICE INDEX ADJUSTMENT 
Commission Staff will calculate the annual change in Producer Price Index (“PPI”), as 
determined by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, that will be allowed to be applied to the 
LPSC’s rates for nonconsensual towing services. The LPSC’s rates will be increased or 
decreased by an amount equal to the annual percentage rate change (rounded to the nearest 
$0.50). The rate change will be posted annually on the LPSC’s website on April 1st, or the 
next business day following. Any rate increase or decrease pursuant to this section shall be 
effective upon posting by the Commission Staff.

The Commission’s General Order dated June 7, 20066 (“2006 General Order”), authorizes 
the imposition of a $25 citation fee when a citation is issued to a Commission-jurisdictional motor 
carrier. 
The Commission Staff’s Case 

At the hearing and in LPSC Staff’s Post-Hearing Brief (“Post-Hearing Brief”), 
Commission Staff alleged that Jace’s Towing violated La. R.S. 45:161 through 180.1 and the 1999 
General Order by operating intrastate without authority, and violated the Towing Order by 
exceeding state prescribed rates contained in the 2025 Towing Order Rates. Commission Staff 
seeks an order: 1) finding the Jace’s Towing guilty as alleged; 2) fining Jace’s Towing $1000 
pursuant to La. R.S. 45:171(C) and 180.1(E) for operating without authority;7 3) requiring Jace’s 
Towing to refund $171.84 to the complainant pursuant to the Towing Order/2025 Towing Order 
Rates;8 and, 4) requiring Jace’s Towing to pay a $25 citation fee per the 2006 General Order. In 
support of its allegations, the Commission Staff presented the testimony of Transportation 
Administrator Tammy Burl. 
Testimony of Tammy Burl 
Ms. Burl testified that as Transportation Administrator she supervises the day-to-day 
operations of the Commission’s Transportation Division, including complaints and investigations 
into carriers who may be operating without authority and exceeding state prescribed rates. Ms. 
Burl testified to her knowledge of applicable statutes and General Orders regarding nonconsensual 
towing. She stated that pursuant to the Towing Order, rates may be increased on April 1 each year 
and the revised rates are posted on the Commission’s website. She stated further that rates were 
increased on April 1, 2025. 

Ms. Burl testified that she was familiar with Jace’s Towing because it was previously 
registered with the Commission as a nonconsensual towing company, but was no longer registered. 
She identified a letter, dated September 27, 2023, to Jace’s Towing stating that it advised the 
Carrier that its LPSC account was closed effective September 25, 2023, and that it was no longer 
allowed to perform nonconsensual tows in Louisiana. Also, that if Jace’s Towing wanted to resume 
operations, the letter provided the steps necessary to reinstate its LPSC authority. Attached to the 
letter was a copy of Order No. T-36898 dated September 25, 2023, ordering the cancellation of 
Common Carrier Certificate No. 7922-A, previously issued to Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s

Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law 
Having considered applicable law and the evidence presented in this case, the Commission 
makes the following findings of fact and conclusions of law: 
Findings of Fact 
1. Jace’s Towing previously held LPSC authority to perform nonconsensual tows through 
Common Carrier Certificate No. 7922-A. Jace’s Towing’s authority was canceled by Order 
No. T-36898 issued on September 25, 2023. 
2. On September 27, 2023, Ms. Burl mailed and emailed a letter to Jace’s Towing explaining 
that its authority had been canceled, it was no longer permitted to conduct nonconsensual 
tows in Louisiana, and the steps necessary to reinstate its authority if it wished to resume 
operations. Attached was a copy of Order No. T-36898 (Staff Exhibit 1, in globo). 
3. Jace’s Towing did not have LPSC authority to perform nonconsensual tows on October 4, 
2025, and as of the date of the hearing, had not obtained authority. 
Order No. T-37789

4. On October 4, 2025, Maegan Cline’s daughter parked a Hyundai Elantra in Opelousas, 
Louisiana to attend an event. 
5. Around 10:19 P.M., upon Ms. Cline’s daughter’s return to the Elantra, Jace’s Towing had 
the Elantra hooked to a tow truck and was in the process of towing or preparing to tow the 
Elantra. 
6. Neither Ms. Cline nor Ms. Cline’s daughter had requested that the Elantra be towed. 
7. Ms. Cline made a payment in the amount of $250 to Rodney Dupre, Jr. through CashApp 
on October 4, 2025, at 10:19 P.M. Ms. Cline later disputed the charge and sought a refund 
through CashApp, but the refund request was denied. (Staff Exhibit 7, in globo). 
8. Upon receiving the $250 payment from Ms. Cline, Jace’s Towing unhooked the Elantra 
from the tow truck and turned the vehicle back over to Ms. Cline’s daughter. 
9. Jace’s Towing Invoice No. 563 was issued for the Elantra tow. (Staff Exhibit 7, in globo). 
10. Ms. Cline electronically submitted the Complaint to the Commission regarding the tow

title: Order No. U-37563 — Utility Order for Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte.
text:
Order No. U-37563
Page 1
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
ORDER NUMBER U-37563
ENTERGY LOUISIANA, LLC, EX PARTE.
Docket No. U-37563, In re: Application for Certification of the Adams Creek-Robert 230kV
Project pursuant to General Order dated September 10, 2024 (Transmission Siting Order).
(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)
ORDER
I.
Overview
On April 21, 2025, Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL” or the “Company”) filed an
Application with the Commission (the “Application”) seeking certification by the Louisiana Public
Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) that the public convenience and necessity would
be served by the completion and siting of a transmission project located on the north shore of Lake
Pontchartrain, in ELL’s Amite South Planning Region (“Amite South”). That project would be
located in Tangipahoa, St. Tammany, and Washington Parishes, and it includes the construction
of a new 41-mile 230kV transmission line from the Adams Creek Substation to the Robert
Substation, as well as substation expansions and upgrades at the Adams Creek Substation, Robert
Substation, Fairview Substation, and Madisonville Substation (together, the “Adams Creek-Robert
230kV Project” or the “Project”). (Ex. ELL-1 at 1). ELL estimates that the project will cost $197.7
million. (Id., at 3). This is a “Class 3” cost estimate which can be up to 20 percent below or 30
percent above the estimated amount, resulting in a possible range of $157 million to $256 million.
(Tr. at 17). The estimated annual revenue requirement based on those estimates is $20.942 million.
(Id.).
The Amite South planning region is a historic load pocket, an area in which there is more
load than available generation to serve that load, and, as a result, transmission is relied upon to
enable needed imports to reliably serve that load. (Tr. at 5). The Project enables a new north-south
path into Washington, St. Tammany, and Tangipahoa Parishes. (Id.). The Adams Creek Project is
the fifth project proposed by ELL addressing issues in Amite South, and it enhances reliability
and other load serving needs on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain, and along the east and west
banks of the Mississippi River. (Id.).
ELL asserted that the Project will provide several benefits. First, it will increase load
serving capability by 100 MW to serve new block load and normal load growth on the North Shore.
Order No. U-37563
Page 2
1 LPSC General Order dated September 10, 2024, In re: Review and Possible Modification of the Commission’s 
General Order dated October 10, 2013 Governing Transmission Certification and General Siting in Docket No. R-
36199.
(Staff Ex. 2 at 6). It will increase operational reliability of the area by preventing thermal overloads
of existing lines when new block loads are added to the system. (Id.). It will provide redundancy
benefits and remedy potential NERC violations. (Id. at 7). It will provide additional flexibility
related to resource planning, by providing additional import capability, and addressing issues that
will arise with anticipated deactivation of generation impacting Amite South and the North Shore.
(Id.). It will provide extreme event resilience; the Project structures are designed to a 150-mph
wind speed rating in St. Tammany and Tangipahoa parishes and 125-mph in Washington Parish.
(Staff Ex. 2 at 7-8; Ex. ELL 5 at 17).
In addition to seeking a certification that the completion and siting of the Project will serve
the public convenience and necessity, ELL requested a finding that the actual retail revenue
requirement associated with the prudently incurred costs of the Project is deemed eligible for
recovery by the Company through the appropriate recovery mechanism at the time that the
components of the Project are placed into service and that the generalized siting of the Project and
its construction is a reasonable and cost-effective solution to provide reliable electric service in
the Amite South Region. (Staff Ex. 2 at 2).
A timely intervention was submitted on behalf of the Louisiana Energy Users Group
("LEUG") on May 2, 2025. On June 4, 2025, the LEUG filed a timely Statement of Objection and
on June 5, 2025, the LPSC Staff filed an Objection Without Prejudice - both in accordance with
the requirements set forth in the General Order dated September 10, 2024 in Docket No. R-36199
("2024 Siting Order").1 On September 16, 2025, the Staff submitted the Direct Testimony of R.
Lane Sisung and the Direct Testimony of John A. Chapman. On September 17, 2025, LEUG
submitted the Direct Testimony of James R. Dauphinais (confidential version and public version).
On October 3, 2025, LEUG submitted the Cross-Answering Testimony of Mr. Dauphinais. On
December 2, 2025, ELL submitted confidential and public versions of the rebuttal testimonies of
Laura K. Beauchamp and Bradley D. Skok. On December 3, 2025, Staff filed a motion to substitute
redacted and confidential versions of the Direct Testimony of R. Lane Sisung, which was granted
on that same date. The hearing in this matter was held before the Administrative Law Judge
(“ALJ”) on February 5, 2026.
Order No. U-37563
Page 3
After post-hearing and post-hearing reply briefs were filed, the “Proposed
Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge” (“Proposed Recommendation”) was issued
on April 16, 2026. That Proposed Recommendation found that the Project was not in the public
interest, and it denied the Company’s Application. 
On May 1, 2026, the Staff and ELL each filed exceptions to the proposed recommendation.
On May 18, 2026, the LEUG filed a reply to the exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation.
On May 21, 2026, the “Final Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge” (“Final
Recommendation”) was issued, which affirmed the Proposed Recommendation. On May 27, 2026,
ELL filed a request for oral argument, and on June 15, 2026 LEUG submitted correspondence to
the Commission in support of the Final Recommendation. The matter was included on the agenda
of the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session for Commission consideration. 
II.
COMMISSION JURISDICTION
The Commission's authority and jurisdiction are specifically set forth in Article IV Section
21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which sets forth in pertinent part:
The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and shall
have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt and enforce
reasonable rules, regulations and procedures necessary for the discharge of its
duties, and perform other duties as provided by law.
III.
STAFF REVIEW
Staff, after conducting a full review of the testimony and discovery responses in this
proceeding, determined that the ELL request for certification is well-supported and can reasonably
be granted. (Staff Ex. 2 at 14). While Staff offered evidence that ELL did not adequately
demonstrate that the Project is required to serve reasonably assumed load growth at this time, the
fact that the project would create a new north to south path into the load pocket and would have
avoided the May 25, 2025 load shed event, combined with the resiliency, flexibility and expanded
future load-serving capability that the Project will provide is sufficient for the Commission to
reasonably conclude that the project could be certified. (Id.; Tr. at 65-66 (Sisung)). Under the
requirements of the 2024 Siting Order, this is sufficient to justify the Project. 
The "Certification and Siting Rules" contained in attachment A to the 2024 Siting Order,
Section IV, addresses the approval standard:
In consideration of any Application required under this Order, the Commission may
approve the Application if it finds the proposed Transmission Facility to be in the
public interest and the interests of affected ratepayers. In making that determination
the Commission may consider the expected impact of such Transmission Facility
Order No. U-37563
Page 4
2 2024 Siting Order, Attach. A, page 5.
on costs, retail rates, service reliability, reduction of congestion, material economic
benefits, the interstate or intrastate benefits to be achieved, and whether the
proposed Transmission Facility is consistent with public policy, including policy
goals of the Commission.2
The "public interest" standard is broad by design. It allows the Commission to consider a wide
range of factors. Those factors include expected benefits, reliability, need, and policy goals. 
The need for this Project is supported by the other many benefits that it will provide. It will
increase load serving capability by 100 MW to serve block load and organic load growth on the
North Shore. (Staff Ex. 2 at 6). It will increase operational reliability of the area by preventing
thermal overloads of existing lines when new block loads are added to the system. (Id.). It will
provide redundancy benefits and remedy potential NERC violations. (Id. at 7). It will provide
additional flexibility related to resource planning, by providing additional import capability and
addressing issues that will arise with anticipated deactivation of generation impacting Amite south
and the North Shore. (Id.). It will provide extreme event resilience; the Project structures are
designed to a 150-mph wind speed rating in St. Tammany and Tangipahoa parishes and 125-mph
in Washington Parish. (Staff Ex. 2 at 7-8; Ex. ELL 5 at 17).
The record demonstrates that the Project, had it been in place at the time, would have
prevented the May 25 load shed event. (Staff Ex. 2 at 10-11). On May 25, 2025 at approximately
4 pm EST thousands of customers in the New Orleans area lost power due to an order by the
Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) to ELL and Cleco to shed 600 MW of
load. (LEUG Ex. No.6 at 8-9 (Staff October 10, 2025 “After-Action Report”)). It was a major
event; about 20% of the load in the New Orleans area was offline. (Tr. at 32-34 (Skok)). While
some customers were restored earlier, it was 8:49 EST before all customers were restored. (LEUG
Ex. 6 at 22-32). The report stated it is “clear that Amite South’s core problem is structural: a
peninsular, corridor dependent grid with limited import ties, so a single high voltage outage or a
cluster of generator outages can tip the area into a post-contingent risk.” (Id., 6 at 42). That report
recommended “continued diligence in seeking prudent transmission projects that are in the public
interest to relieve the risks associated with load sheds in the Amite South load pocket.” (Id. at 43.)
It also indicated that the Adams Creek-Robert 230 kV line would provide relief to the conditions
the triggered the Temporary IROL. (Id.). The Project will relieve the risks associated with the May
25 load shed event. 
Order No. U-37563
Page 5
Further, there are legacy generators in the region that are nearing the end of their useful
lives and are scheduled to retire in the near future. (Tr. at 6 (Beauchamp)). Ninemile Units 4 and
5 and Little Gypsy Units 2 and 3 are scheduled to retire between 2026 and 2032. (Tr. at 16
(Beauchamp)). The Project will provide some relief by increasing load serving capability by 100
MW to serve load and load growth on the North Shore. (Staff Ex. 2 at 6). It will increase
operational reliability of the area by preventing thermal overloads of existing lines when new block
loads are added to the system. (Id.). It will provide redundancy benefits and remedy potential
NERC violations. (Id. at 7
In addition, there are some uncontested issues in this matter that are supported by all parties
and the evidence submitted. First, ELL’s Application complied with the requirements of Section
V of General Order No. R-36199 dated September 10, 2024. Second, the generalized siting and
commencement of construction for the Adams Creek –Robert 230kV Project, as described in the
Company’s Application, testimony, and exhibits, are appropriate and reasonable.
Third, while ELL did not request that any component of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV project
be deemed exempt under Section VIII of the 2024 Siting Order, certain components of the Adams
Creek – Robert 230kV Project, as described in the Company’s Application, testimony, and
exhibits, qualify for exemption from Commission certification pursuant to the 2024 Siting Order.
Specifically, the expansion of the Adams Creek Substation, expansion of the Robert Substation,
upgrades at the Fairview Substation, upgrades at the Cleco Power, LLC-owned Madisonville
Substation, and placement of distribution lines to accommodate the new 230kV transmission lines
qualify for exemption from Commission certification pursuant to Section VIII(a) of the 2024 Siting
Order and/or do not fall within the definition of “Transmission Facilities” in the 2024 Siting Order.
Fourth, Staff recommended reporting requirements that are uncontested. Under those
requirements the Company will file the requisite construction reports under Section VI of the 2024
Siting Order related to all components of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV Project (i.e., the
substation projects, distribution lines, and Project transmission facilities), including those
components that may or may not individually qualify for exemption from certification under the
Commission’s 2024 Siting Order. Additionally, ELL will file a report with the Commission within
120 days after completion of the in-service date of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV Project.
Further, during the construction period and until the in-service dates of the ASTP projects, ELL
agrees to provide the Commission and Intervenors in this proceeding with any changes to its
Order No. U-37563
Page 6
proposed strategic generation and transmission projects affecting the Amite South region and/or
to the material assumptions or conclusions of its ASTP studies reasonably promptly after the
occurrence of such change. If there is a material change in the proposed projects or any of the
material assumptions or conclusions of the ASTP studies, the Commission should be made
immediately aware of such changes and why such changes were not reasonably knowable at the
time of the certification decisions and how ELL proposes to address any impacts those changes
may present.
IV. COMMISSION CONSIDERATION
This matter was considered by the Commission at its June 17, 2026 Business and Executive
Session. Chairman Skrmetta made the following motion:
It is my view that the benefits of the project exceed the costs. It will not only provide an
additional north-south route into the Amite South load pocket, but it will also provide an
additional 100 MW of load serving and import capability. The project will also increase
reliability and prevent thermal overloads as block loads are added to the system in the
future. It will provide increased extreme weather event resilience. And, had the project
been in service at the time, it would have prevented the May 25, 2025 load shed event.
Therefore, I move that the Commission reject the Final Recommendation of the
Administrative Law Judge and find that the Adams-Creek to Robert 230 kV Project is in
the public interest, its siting and completion will serve the public convenience and
necessity, and the project complies with the requirements of the Commission’s 2024 Siting
Order dated September 10, 2024. In addition, Staff testimony recommended various
reporting requirements in its direct testimony, which were not contested. This approval
adopts Staff’s recommended reporting requirements filed into the record on September 16,
2025. Specifically, those requirements are referenced at pp. 17-18 of the Direct Testimony
of R. Lane Sisung and pp. 21-23 of the Direct Testimony of John A. Chapman. 
Chairman Skrmetta’s motion was seconded by Commissioner Francis. With Vice
Chairman Coussan and Commissioner Lewis concurring, and Commissioner Campbell absent, the
Commission voted to reject the Final Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge and
approve the Application for Certification of the Adams Creek-Robert 230kV Project, subject to
certain conditions contained in Staff’s recommendation.
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:
1. The Adams Creek–Robert 230kV Project serves the public convenience and necessity
and is in the public interest and in the interests of affected ratepayers in accordance
with the Commission’s 2024 Siting Order.
2. ELL’s Application complies with the requirements of Section V of General Order
Order No. U-37563
Page 7
No. R-36199 dated September 10, 2024 (the “2024 Siting Order”).
3. The generalized siting and commencement of construction for the Adams Creek –
Robert 230kV Project, as described in the Company’s Application, Testimony, and
Exhibits, are appropriate and reasonable.
4. Certain components of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV Project, as described in the
Company’s Application, Testimony, and Exhibits, qualify for exemption from
Commission certification pursuant to the 2024 Siting Order. Specifically, the expansion
of the Adams Creek Substation, expansion of the Robert Substation, upgrades at the
Fairview Substation, upgrades at the Cleco Power, LLC-owned Madisonville
Substation, and placement of distribution lines to accommodate the new 230kV
transmission lines qualify for exemption from Commission certification pursuant to
Section VIII(a) of the 2024 Siting Order and/or do not fall within the definition of
“Transmission Facilities” in the 2024 Siting Order.
5. The retail revenue requirement associated with the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV
Project is deemed eligible for recovery through ELL’s Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”) to
the extent the Company remains subject to one, or, in the alternative where there is no
FRP in place, that the Commission should authorize the creation of a regulatory asset
until such time that the prudently incurred costs are approved to be reflected in rates in
order to mitigate the effects of regulatory lag.
6. The certification is not a determination of the prudence of the final costs of the Project.
The Company has an ongoing obligation to manage prudently the Adams Creek –
Robert 230kV Project, including ongoing construction and costs. The Company will
submit the final costs of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV Project in the normal
ratemaking process, and only the prudently incurred costs are eligible for recovery.
7. The Company will file the requisite construction reports under Section VI of the 2024
Siting Order related to all components of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV Project
(i.e., the substation projects, distribution lines, and Project transmission facilities),
including those components that may or may not individually qualify for exemption
from certification under the Commission’s 2024 Siting Order. Additionally, ELL will
file a report with the Commission within 120 days after completion of the in-service
date of the Adams Creek – Robert 230kV Project. Further, during the construction
period and until the in-service dates of the ASTP projects, ELL agrees to provide the
Commission and Intervenors in this proceeding with any changes to its proposed
strategic generation and transmission projects affecting the Amite South region and/or
to the material assumptions or conclusions of its ASTP studies reasonably promptly
after the occurrence of such change. If there is a material change in the proposed
projects or any of the material assumptions or conclusions of the ASTP studies, the
Order No. U-37563
Page 8
Commission should be made immediately aware of such changes and why such
changes were not reasonably knowable at the time of the certification decisions and
how ELL proposes to address any impacts those changes may present.
8. This order is effective immediately.

July 9, 2026

CHAIRMAN ERIC F. SKRMETTA

Company advising that the Carrier’s BI & PD insurance would be canceled effective 
February 3, 2026.

regular mail to the Carrier at its address on file with the Commission advising that its

immediately until replacement coverage was submitted.

prepared a tentative hearing letter to the Carrier advising that if a replacement Form E

a hearing on the matter had been tentatively scheduled for June 11, 2026. She mailed 
the letter via USPS regular mail and emailed it to the Carrier to its respective addresses 
on file with the Commission. Attached was a copy of the notice of cancellation letter.

Ms. Burl issued a citation to the Carrier directing it to appear at a hearing on June 11, 
2026. Attached to the citation were the letters dated February 6, 2026, and March 13, 
2026.

1. At the hearing, the Commission Staff had the burden of proving its allegations against 
the Carrier. Because the Carrier did not appear, the Commission Staff also had the 
burden of demonstrating that the Carrier was provided fair notice of the hearing and the 
opportunity to present a defense. La. R.S. 45:166(A) provides that a certificate may be 
revoked “after notice and hearing for failure to comply with any provision of R.S. 
45:161 through 45:172, or with any lawful order, rule or regulation of the [C]ommission

2. Pursuant to its constitutional and statutory authority, the Commission adopted the Rules 
of Practice and Procedure. Commission Rules 7 and 19 provide for notice of non-
criminal proceedings through publication in the Commission’s Official Bulletin, as well 
as by service “through any means whereby proof of receipt or unclaimed status can be 
shown” to “the last known place of address of the person entitled to receive such notice 
. . . .”14 
3. Pursuant to constitutional and legislative mandate, and Commission orders adopted 
pursuant thereto, the Commission has the authority to regulate motor carriers and to 
ensure that they maintain levels of insurance required by statute and by Commission 
General Orders. The 2023 General Order provides that liability insurance shall be made

and possible revision to the Commission’s Rules.

on a Form E. La. R.S. 45:166(A) states the Commission may revoke a carrier’s authority 
for failure to comply with Commission rules.

that the Carrier received notice of the hearing and Commission Staff’s allegations, 
chiefly the Ruling on Joint Motion to Continue and Notice of Rescheduled Date noting 
the appearance by Midas Touch when the matter was called on June 11, 2026, and its 
joint motion with Commission Staff to continue the hearing to July 9, 2026. Thus, the 
Carrier had the opportunity to appear and present a defense.

cancellation date stated in the Form K. 
6. We find that the Carrier failed to maintain the required proof of insurance coverage 
filing (a Form E) on file with the Commission as required by the 2023 General Order.

through a Form E constitutes a failure to comply with applicable law and Commission 
orders. Therefore, cancellation of the Carrier’s Common Carrier Certificates is 
warranted pursuant to La. R.S. 45:166(A). 
8. The 2006 General Order allows for the imposition of a $25 fee for the issuance of a 
citation by the Commission. Therefore, it is appropriate to require the Carrier to pay the 
$25 citation fee. 
Conclusion 

In accordance with the findings of fact and conclusions of law stated above: 
IT IS ORDERED that Common Carrier Certificate No. 7507-A, currently issued to DTK 
Enterprises, LLC dba Midas Touch Towing, is CANCELED due to the failure of DTK Enterprises,

Commission.

as by service “through any means whereby proof of receipt or unclaimed status can be 
shown” to “the last known place of address of the person entitled to receive such notice 
. . . .”13 
3. Pursuant to constitutional and legislative mandate, and Commission orders adopted 
pursuant thereto, the Commission has the authority to regulate motor carriers and to 
ensure that they maintain levels of insurance required by statute and by Commission 
General Orders. The 2023 General Order provides that liability insurance shall be made 
on a Form E. La. R.S. 45:166(A) states the Commission may revoke a carrier’s authority 
for failure to comply with Commission rules. 
4. The Commission Staff demonstrated through documentary and testimonial evidence, 
chiefly the USPS Tracking results for certified mail tracking number ending in 614144, 
that the Carrier received notice of the hearing and the Commission Staff’s allegations. 
Thus, the Carrier had the opportunity to appear and present a defense. 
5. The Commission Staff proved that the Carrier failed to provide a Form E indicating that 
its BI & PD liability insurance coverage had been extended beyond the March 10, 2026 
cancellation date stated in the Form K. 
6. We find that the Carrier failed to maintain the required proof of insurance coverage 
filing (a Form E) on file with the Commission as required by the 2023 General Order. 
Accordingly, we find that the Carrier is guilty of violating the 2023 General Order. 
7. We conclude that the Carrier’s failure to maintain proof of effective insurance coverage 
through a Form E constitutes a failure to comply with applicable law and Commission 
orders. Therefore, cancellation of the Carrier’s Common Carrier Certificate is warranted 
pursuant to La. R.S. 45:166(A). 
8. The 2006 General Order allows for the imposition of a $25 fee for the issuance of a 
citation by the Commission. Therefore, it is appropriate to require the Carrier to pay the 
$25 citation fee. 
Conclusion 

In accordance with the findings of fact and conclusions of law stated above: 
IT IS ORDERED that Common Carrier Certificate No. 8245, currently issued to Smith 
Towing of Minden LA LLC, is CANCELED due to the failure of Smith Towing of Minden LA 
LLC to maintain proof of insurance coverage on file with the Commission.

Overview
The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission”), having reviewed and considered

filed into the record on May 1, 2026, and a copy of the Draft Order was attached thereto as Exhibit
A.

and recovered by Entex through the purchased gas adjustment (“PGA”) mechanism during the
audit period were reasonable, prudent, and necessary for the provision of natural gas service to its
customers. The Staff Audit Report further found that Entex’s PGA filings during the audit period
complied with the requirements of the PGA General Order and followed the methodology outlined
in Appendix B of the Order. Staff did not identify any ineligible costs that were passed through
the PGA mechanism for recovery by Entex. As a test of reasonableness, Staff found that the
commodity prices for purchased gas paid by the Company tracked the monthly Henry Hub Index
prices. Staff concluded that the Company’s purchased gas supply during the audit period was
reasonable and competitively priced.

recommendation that the Commission should find that the costs incurred and included for recovery

submitted under the requirements of the PGA General Order should be approved.

IV, Section 21(B) of the Louisiana Constitution, which provides the following:

utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.

procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

develop standards governing the ratemaking treatment of purchased gas costs incurred by gas
utilities subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission. Pursuant to the PGA General Order, Entex
was a Group I Company and was required to file PGA schedules on a monthly basis as soon as
practically possible after the first of each month, with supporting documentation for all data inputs,
which were then used for the applicable billing month.

audit period of January 2023 through March 31, 2025, were reasonable, prudent, and
necessary for the provision of natural gas service to customers.
2. Entex’s PGA filings for the audit period of January 2023 through March 31, 2025,
complied with the PGA General Order and followed the methodology outlined in
Appendix B of the Order.
3. No ineligible costs were passed through the PGA mechanism for recovery by Entex
during the audit period of January 2023 through March 31, 2025.

Docket No. T-37844, In Re: Alleged violation of Louisiana Revised Statue 45:168 and General
Orders dated July 01, 1921, as amended, April 03, 2008, as amended, and July 12, 2013 by
exceeding rates as outlined in the company’s tariff dated May 23, 2019, while operating under
Common Carrier Certificate No. 7508-A allegedly having occurred on or about June 27, 2025.
(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session)
I.
Background
In response to a complaint, the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or
“Commission”) Staff opened an investigation into Keep It Moving Services, LLC, (“Keep It
Moving” or “Carrier”) and its business activities. As a result of this investigation, Staff found
evidence that Keep It Moving violated Louisiana Revised Statue 45:168 and General Orders dated
July 01, 1921 as amended, April 03, 2008, as amended, and July 12, 2013 by exceeding rates as
outlined in the Keep It Moving’s tariff dated May 23, 2019, while operating under Common
Carrier Certificate No. 7508-A on or about June 27, 2025. Staff subsequently issued a citation to
Keep It Moving in the present docket.
II.
Jurisdiction
The Commission exercises jurisdiction over common carriers and public utilities in Louisiana
pursuant to Article IV, Section 21(B) of the Louisiana Constitution, which states:
“The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.”
Pursuant to this authority, the Commission has issued General Order dated March 16, 2021,
which provides for the requirements a household goods carrier must satisfy to operate within the
State of Louisiana, and General Order dated April 3, 2008, as amended, which requires that all
household goods carriers operating intrastate in Louisiana must include their legal and/or
registered name and physical address in all advertising. Also, pursuant to this authority, the
Commission issued General Order dated July 12, 2013 adhering to the rates as outlined in the
company’s Commission approved tariff pursuant to General Order dated July 01, 2021 as
amended.
Order No. T-37844
Page 2
Further, LA. R.S. 45:164(E) provides that “[a]ll intrastate movers of household goods shall be
required to apply for and secure a common carrier certificate from the Louisiana Public Service
Commission … prior to engaging in any activities related to moving household goods.”
III.
Stipulation
In response to the citation, Jon-Michael Burns, president of the Carrier, executed an Affidavit
and Stipulation on behalf of the Carrier admitting to violating all listed violations within the
citation. In the Affidavit and Stipulation, Mr. Burns agreed to the imposition of a $1,000.00 fine
and a $25.00 citation fee, with $500.00 of the fine suspended conditioned on the following
conditions: 
1. Agree to refund the charges in the amount of $74.58 for moving services paid by the
customer on October 6, 2025. Such refund will be paid to the customer, Michael Mann, by
certified funds and mailed to the customer using priority mail to 150 E Palmetto Park Road;
Suite 518; Boca Raton, FL 33432 on or before May 3, 2026;
2. Agree to provide the LPSC proof of the aforementioned refund, by submitting a copy of
the certified fund and proof priority mailing, totaling $74.58, on or before May 3, 2026;
3. Agree that the company shall follow the Commission’s rules and regulations regarding the
providing of estimates for regulated household goods moving services, including the
estimated number of hours for the move, pursuant to the Commission’s General Order
dated July 12, 2013 and adhering to the rates as outlined in the company’s Commission
approved tariff pursuant to General Order dated July 01, 2021 as amended and;
4. Remit payment due in certified funds in the amount of $525.00 payable to the LPSC and
deliver with this executed stipulated agreement to the LPSC to be received in the LPSC
office no later than 4:30 p.m. on May 3, 2026. 
Failure to comply with any of the above requirements will result in the $500.00 suspended 
portion of the fine becoming due immediately.
IV.
Commission Action
This matter was considered at the Commission’s June 17, 2026 Business and Executive
Session. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, with Chairman
Coussan and Commissioner Francis concurring, and Commissioner Campbell absent, the

Commission voted to assert its original and primary jurisdiction and take the matter up pursuant
to Rule 57.
On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, with Vice Chairman
Coussan and Commissioner Francis concurring, and Commissioner Campbell absent, the
Commission voted to accept the Affidavit and Stipulation executed on May 4, 2026 for fines and
fees totaling $525.00.
